children: Booming demand for data-center cooling equipment helped Aaon deliver a blowout earnings report and raise its annual outlook. But Wall Street sees another reason for optimism: Its traditional heating and air-conditioning operations are showing strength, too.
Aaons stock surged on Tuesday 23% to $77.31, putting it on pace for its largest daily percent increase since May, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The company on Monday reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of 83 cents a share, exceeding consensus calls for 57 cents, according to FactSet. Revenue rose 84% year over year to a record $707 million, surpassing projections for $601 million.

Aaon raised its full-year revenue growth forecast to between 72% and 75%, up from its previous outlook of 55% to 60%. The company also increased its gross margin forecast to about 26%, from a previous range of 25% to 26%.

Much of the growth came from Aaon's emerging data-center cooling business. Sales of its BASX-branded products surged 218% year over year to $397.2 million, fueled by demand for specialized cooling systems that prevent powerful computer systems from overheating.
Aaon's Coil Products segment also benefited from strong demand for liquid-cooling equipment, which uses circulating fluids to remove heat from data center hardware.
That was the headline, but Aaon's core HVAC business had a strong quarter of its own.

Its Oklahoma operations, which primarily manufacture rooftop heating and cooling systems for commercial buildings, reported a 19% increase in sales to $283 million, well above the 5% growth forecast by D.A. Davidson.

D.A. Davidson analysts said the stronger-than-expected performance reflected improvements in Aaon's manufacturing operations, including fewer production bottlenecks and better quality controls. They maintained a Buy rating for Aaon and a $110 price target, implying 75% upside from Monday's closing price of $62.87.

Those improvements also helped Aaon fulfill orders more quickly. The company's order backlog reached $1.85 billion at the end of the third quarter, up 40% from a year earlier, although it declined sequentially as production increased.
KeyBanc Capital Markets was more cautious, noting that the backlog for BASX-branded products declined 5% sequentially, even as it grew 51% year over year.
KeyBanc analysts also suggested that part of Aaon's higher margin outlook could reflect accounting restatements, not just stronger operating performance.

The company revised its first-half financial results after identifying a material weakness in its internal controls, increasing previously reported revenue by $10.7 million and earnings per share by 9 cents.
The analysts highlighted how the rapid expansion of Aaon's BASX operations is limiting margin improvement, as the company incurs additional costs to support growing demand.
